steps.title: Putting it all together
body: You've learned four verb forms, five particles, and 33 words, each introduced in a real sentence.
This review summarizes the patterns, revisits the vocabulary, and finishes with a 12-question assessment that mixes all three sections.
After the assessment, the final page shows which concepts to revisit and links back to the lessons that teach them.

steps.title: The four forms
points: Present -아/어/해: habits, general facts, and things happening around now.
Future -(으)ㄹ 거야: plans, intentions, and predictions.
Progressive -고 있어: an action underway right now.

table.caption: One verb, four forms: 공부하다 (to study)

steps.title: The five particles
points: Particles attach to the end of a noun to show its role.
Most have a vowel form and a consonant form; 에 and 에서 never change.
In casual speech, 은/는, 이/가, and 을/를 are often dropped when the meaning is clear.

steps.title: Vocabulary review: verbs
steps.intro: All fifteen verbs from this module. Can you give the present, past, future, and progressive of each?

steps.title: Vocabulary review: people, places, and things
Vocabulary review: pronouns, time, and place words
Module assessment
steps.intro: Twelve mixed questions from all three sections. Your first answer to each question counts toward your score; you can still retry to see the explanation.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: 나는 물을 ___. (I drink water.)
questions.explanation: The present of 마시다 is 마셔 (마시 + 어). 마셨어 is past and 마실 거야 is future.

questions.prompt: Which sentence means "I ate a meal"?
questions.explanation: 먹었어 is the past of 먹다. 먹어 is present, and 먹고 있어 means "am eating."

questions.prompt: What is the future form of 가다 (to go)?
questions.explanation: 가 ends in a vowel, so ㄹ attaches under it: 갈 거야 (gal geoya).

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: 나는 지금 책을 ___. (I am reading a book now.)
questions.explanation: An action in progress uses -고 있어: 읽고 있어.

options.text: I will meet a friend tomorrow.

questions.explanation: 어제 = yesterday, 친구를 = friend (object), 만났어 = met.

questions.prompt: Which particle marks the place where an action happens?
questions.explanation: 에서 marks the location of an action (집에서 일해). 에 marks a destination (학교에 가).

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: 나는 내일 학교___ 갈 거야. (I will go to school tomorrow.)
questions.explanation: School is the destination of going, so it takes 에: 학교에 갈 거야.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: 나는 커피___ 살 거야. (I will buy coffee.)
questions.explanation: Coffee is the object, and 커피 ends in a vowel, so it takes 를: 커피를.

questions.prompt: Which form of 일하다 (to work) is progressive?
questions.explanation: -고 있어 marks the progressive: 일하고 있어 = am working. The others are present, past, and future.
기다리 + 었어 contracts to 기다렸어 (gidaryeosseo), the past tense.

questions.prompt: Tap the word that shows where you will apply.

sentence.english: I will apply to that company.

questions.explanation: 회사에 carries 에, which marks the target of applying. 그 (that) describes 회사 but is not the particle-marked word.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to say "I am waiting for a friend here."

sentence.english: I am waiting for a friend here.

questions.explanation: The verb goes last. 여기서 marks where, 친구를 is who you are waiting for, and -고 있어 shows it's happening now.

steps.title: Optional challenge: one verb, four sentences
steps.intro: Pick any verb from this module and make four sentences with it: present, past, future, and progressive. Then compare your sentences with the model answer.

questions.prompt: Choose a verb and say or write four sentences: present, past, future, and progressive.

answer.korean: 나는 커피를 마셔. / 나는 어제 커피를 마셨어. / 나는 내일 커피를 마실 거야. / 나는 지금 커피를 마시고 있어.
answer.romanization: Naneun keopireul masyeo. / Naneun eoje keopireul masyeosseo. / Naneun naeil keopireul masil geoya. / Naneun jigeum keopireul masigo isseo.
answer.english: I drink coffee. / I drank coffee yesterday. / I will drink coffee tomorrow. / I am drinking coffee now.

questions.explanation: Model answer using 마시다. Check that your verb is last, that each ending matches its tense, and that your object has 을/를 (or is left bare, as in casual speech).

steps.title: Module 1 complete
points: You can form the casual present, past, future, and progressive of everyday verbs.
You can use 은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 에, and 에서 in short sentences.
You know 33 words, each learned and practiced in context.
